cards.front: What is a Playwright fixture?
cards.back: Named setup that a test requests in its parameters. The runner builds it, passes it in, and cleans it up afterwards.

cards.front: What do fixtures offer over `beforeEach` hooks?
cards.back: They run only when requested, keep setup next to cleanup, and can be reused across files.

cards.front: Which built-in fixtures are test-scoped, and which are worker-scoped?
cards.back: `page`, `context`, and `request` are test-scoped. `browser`, `browserName`, and `playwright` are worker-scoped.

cards.front: If tests share a browser, where does their isolation come from?
cards.back: Each test gets a new browser context, with its own cookies and storage.

cards.front: How do you add a custom fixture?
cards.back: Call `base.extend({ name: async ({ deps }, use) => { ... } })` and import the returned `test` in your specs.

cards.front: What does `await use(value)` do in a fixture?
cards.back: It hands the value to the test and waits for the test to finish. Code after it is the cleanup.

cards.front: What goes wrong if you forget `await` before `use()`?
cards.back: The cleanup code runs before the test body, and the test can still pass without any error.

cards.front: How does a fixture with no dependencies declare its first parameter?
cards.back: As `{}`, as in `async ({}, use) => { ... }`. Playwright requires the object destructuring pattern there.

cards.front: How do you declare a worker-scoped fixture?
cards.back: Use a tuple: `name: [async ({}, use) => { ... }, { scope: 'worker' }]`. Worker types go in the second generic of `extend`.

cards.front: Can a worker-scoped fixture depend on `page` or `request`?
cards.back: No. Worker fixtures can depend only on worker fixtures, so build a context from `browser` or `playwright`.

cards.front: In what order are fixtures set up and torn down?
cards.back: Set up in dependency order, and torn down in reverse.

cards.front: What happens to worker fixtures when a test fails?
cards.back: The worker process is replaced, so its worker fixtures are torn down and set up again in the new one.

cards.front: Why use `parallelIndex` instead of `workerIndex` to pick an account?
cards.back: `workerIndex` goes up after every restart. `parallelIndex` stays between 0 and `workers - 1`.

cards.front: Why can't `beforeAll` use the `page` fixture?
cards.back: `page` and `context` are created per test, and `beforeAll` runs outside any single test.

cards.front: How do you stop a slow fixture from using up the test's timeout?
cards.back: Give it its own limit: `[fn, { timeout: 60_000 }]`. Test-scoped fixtures otherwise share the test's timeout.

cards.front: What does `{ auto: true }` do?
cards.back: It runs the fixture for every test, even when no test asks for it.

cards.front: How do you make a fixture value configurable per file or `describe` block?
cards.back: Define it as `['default', { option: true }]`, then change it with `test.use({ name: value })`.

cards.front: How do you combine fixtures from several files?
cards.back: Call `mergeTests(testA, testB)` and export the result.

cards.front: How do you override a built-in fixture such as `page`?
cards.back: Define a fixture with the same name in `extend`. It can request the original, as in `page: async ({ page }, use) => { ... }`.

cards.front: Why listen to `pageerror` as well as `console`?
cards.back: Uncaught exceptions fire `pageerror`, and they don't appear as console events.

cards.front: How can a test detect an image that returns 200 but is corrupt?
cards.back: Check that `img.complete` is true and `img.naturalWidth` is greater than 0 in the browser.
